task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm hoping you can help me out. My phone has been showing "No Service" for the past few hours now, and I can't make calls or use data. I'm not really sure what happened — it was working fine earlier today.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry to hear you've lost service — let's get this sorted out.

To start, I'll need to pull up your account. Could you please confirm one of the following:

- **The phone number on the line that's having trouble**, or
- **Your full name and date of birth** so I can look up your account that way

Once I've verified your account, I can check the status of your line and see whether it's something on our end (like a suspension or a billing issue) or something we can troubleshoot on the device itself.
turns.execution_output: User: Sure thing — my name is John Smith, and the phone number on the line that's having trouble is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought: I found your account, John. Let me check the details of the line with that number.

turns.thought:
Thanks for confirming — I've pulled up your account, John. Here's what I'm seeing on our end:

- **Line 555-123-2002 (L1002):** Status is **Active** — no suspension
- **Account (C1001):** Active, in good standing
- **Bills:** The February bill (B1002, $150.00) is issued and not yet marked overdue; the January bill is paid in full
- **Data usage:** 8.7 GB of your 15 GB Premium Plan limit — well under the cap, so data shouldn't be cut off
- **Roaming:** Already enabled on this line

So nothing on our side is blocking your service. That means the "No Service" issue is most likely coming from the device itself.

Let me work through a few device checks with you. First, could you tell me **what you currently see at the top of your screen (the status bar)**? Specifically:

1. Is there an **airplane icon (✈️)** showing?
2. Do you see any **signal bars** at all, or does it say **"No Signal" / "SOS" / "Searching..."**?
3. Do you see a network type like **5G / 4G / LTE**?

Also, if it's easy to do: could you swipe down into your quick settings and confirm whether **Airplane Mode** is ON or OFF? If it happens to be ON, please toggle it OFF and let me know whether the signal comes back.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at my screen for you.

turns.thought:
Good — Airplane Mode was the right first thing to rule out, and it's now off. Since the line itself is Active and there are no billing blocks, let's work through the device side.

**Next step: restart your phone.**

A full reboot (power off, wait ~30 seconds, power back on) refreshes the phone's connection to the network and clears a lot of temporary glitches. Please do that now, and once it comes back up, take a look at the status bar again and tell me what you see.

While you're in there, one more thing to check:

**Mobile data is currently turned OFF** (your status bar showed "Data Disabled"). After the restart, go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network** (or "Cellular") and make sure the **Mobile Data** toggle is switched ON. Once we get your signal back, that's also required for picture/video messaging to work.

Please let me know after the restart:
1. Do you now see **signal bars** and a network type (**5G / 4G / LTE**)?
2. Does it still say **"No Signal"**?
3. Does it show anything about the **SIM card** — e.g. "No SIM card detected" or "SIM locked"?

If the signal doesn't come back after the restart, the next most likely culprit is the SIM card itself, and I'll walk you through re-seating it and resetting your APN settings.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me restart the phone now.

turns.thought:
Great instinct — and yes, let's keep going one step at a time.

**Don't turn Mobile Data on just yet.** Mobile data needs a working cellular connection underneath it, so while you're on "No Signal" that toggle won't bring anything back — and switching it now could make it harder to tell what actually fixed things later. We'll flip it on as soon as we see signal bars.

**Next step: re-seat your SIM card.** This is the most common fix for a phone that was working fine and then suddenly dropped to no service — the card can shift slightly out of contact.

1. Power the phone **completely off**
2. Locate the **SIM tray** (usually a small pinhole on the side) and eject it with a SIM tool or a straightened paperclip
3. Take the card out, check for any **dirt, smudges, or damage** on the gold contacts, and wipe it gently with a dry cloth
4. Re-insert it so it sits **flat and snug** in the tray, then push the tray fully back in
5. Power the phone back on and check the status bar

One thing to confirm first: your device is a **Smartphone Pro Max**, which supports **eSIM**, and your line's device was activated on 2025-02-15 (with an eSIM transfer recorded prior to that). Do you know if this line is running on a **physical SIM card or an eSIM**? If it's an eSIM, there's no card to re-seat — you'd instead go to **Settings → Network & Internet → SIMs**, toggle the line **off**, wait about 30 seconds, then toggle it **back on**.

Two quick questions while you're at it:

- **Are any other phones on your account working right now?** (For example the 555-123-2001 or 555-123-2003 lines.) If those have service too, that tells us the problem is isolated to your device rather than a coverage issue in your area.
- **Did anything happen right before this started** — dropped phone, new case, or a location change?

Let me know what the status bar shows after re-seating (or toggling) the SIM, and we'll go from there. If that doesn't do it, our next stop is your **APN settings**, which we can reset to default — those can also knock out service when they get corrupted.

One unrelated note so it's on your radar: your February bill ($150.00) was due 2/19 and still shows unpaid — it hasn't affected your service, but let me know if you'd like to take care of that as well.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me re-seat the SIM card now.

turns.thought:
No problem — let's keep going. And absolutely, APN is the right next step. Corrupted APN settings are a very common cause of exactly this: line is Active, SIM is fine, but the phone can't register on the network.

First, let me check one thing on my end.

Yes — APN settings are exactly the right next step. That's three common causes ruled out (Airplane Mode, reboot, SIM), and a corrupted APN is the next most likely thing to knock out service with no SIM error showing.

**Next step: reset your APN settings to default.**

1. Open **Settings**
2. Go to **Network & Internet** → **Mobile Network** (may be called "Cellular" on your device)
3. Tap **Advanced** (if you see it), then **Access Point Names**
4. Look for the **menu (⋮ three dots)** in the top-right corner and tap **Reset to default**
5. You should see a confirmation — accept it

**Important:** after resetting, you'll need to **fully restart the phone** again (power off, wait ~30 seconds, power on) for the change to take effect. The settings don't apply properly until after a reboot.

Once it's back up, check the status bar and let me know:
1. Any **signal bars** and a **network type** (5G / 4G / LTE)?
2. Still **"No Signal"**?

**One more diagnostic that would really help narrow this down.** When iOS or Android hits a SIM problem that a re-seat doesn't fix, there's usually a SIM status message hidden in settings that doesn't appear in the status bar:

- **Android:** Settings → **About Phone** → **Status** → **SIM status**. Tell me if it says **Active / Ready**, **No SIM**, or something about a **PIN/PUK**. Or: Settings → Network & Internet → **SIMs** — is your line listed there at all, and is its toggle ON?
- **iPhone:** Settings → **General** → **About**. Scroll to the bottom — do you see any entry for your line, or an **IMEI**?

That tells us whether the phone is talking to the card at all.

I also ran a check on your other lines while you were doing that. For your reference:
- **555-123-2001** — Active, working normally on our end
- **555-123-2002** (yours) — Active, in good standing
- **555-123-2003** — Currently **Suspended** (since Feb 1), which is why there's a $5 suspension fee on the February bill

That further confirms your line itself is provisioned correctly and the issue is on the device.

So: reset APN → full restart → check status bar (and the SIM status screen if you can). Let me know what you see, and if it's still "No Signal" I'll get you connected with our technical support team for the deeper hardware/line-level diagnostics.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me reset the APN settings now.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's the root cause. A SIM locked with a PIN will show "No Signal" and will not register on the network until it's unlocked. That's why Airplane Mode, the reboot, and re-seating the SIM all had no effect.

**You just need to enter the PIN once, and service will come back.** The phone has been prompting for it (likely at the lock screen or on boot) and it's been sitting there waiting.

**What to try:**

1. **Reboot or lock/unlock the phone** to bring up the SIM PIN prompt. Depending on your device it appears either at boot with a message like *"Enter SIM PIN"* or *"SIM locked — contact your carrier,"* or as a notification you can tap.
2. **Enter the PIN** and confirm. Once accepted, the status bar should pick up signal immediately — no restart needed.

**If you don't know the PIN:**

- Look for the **default PIN** printed on the original **SIM card packaging** or paperwork from when the line was activated.
- Check whether it's saved in your **password manager**, or in **Settings → Security → SIM card lock** (on Android this is where you'd have set it, though it won't show you the existing PIN).

**How many attempts you get:** you typically get **3 attempts** before the SIM locks to a PUK code. This is the part I want to be careful about, because a wrong PIN costs you an attempt.

**If you're unsure of the PIN — stop and don't guess.** My recommendation: try it only if you're confident you know it. If you exhaust the attempts, the SIM locks to a **PUK-locked** state, and at that point a re-seat or reset won't help.

Let me flag this clearly: **if you've tried the PIN and it doesn't work, tell me right away and don't try again.** PUK/SIM security matters can't be resolved by me — they need our technical support team, who can verify your identity and issue the PUK code. I'd rather hand you to them with an unlocked SIM than have you locked out with two attempts burned.

So: give the PIN a try if you have it, or let me know if you don't and I'll transfer you to technical support to get it reset. Also let me know whether you run into the prompt at all — if the phone isn't offering a way to enter it, that's a different problem we'll want to look at.
turns.execution_output:
User: I appreciate the warning about the attempts — I definitely don't want to lock myself out completely.

The thing is, I have no idea what the SIM PIN is. I don't remember ever setting one up, and I don't have the original SIM packaging or paperwork anymore — it's been a while since this line was activated. I checked and it's not saved anywhere I can find either.

Given what you said about only getting 3 attempts before it locks to a PUK code, I'm not going to guess at it. That seems like a good way to make this worse.

So I think I do need to be handed off to your technical support team to get this reset. Can you transfer me to them?
